title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026

Reason for Admission: Abdominal pain and lack of bowel movements following new medication.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight loss.
Gastrointestinal: Positive for abdominal distension and decreased bowel sounds.
Neurological: Negative for confusion or weakness.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.

HPI: Patient is a 77-year-old woman who reports a gradual onset of abdominal discomfort and cessation of bowel movements. She recently started a new medication regimen. She reports generalized bloating and discomfort in the mid-abdomen.

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for an ileus. Imaging and physical examination were performed to evaluate for any surgical emergencies. Clinical assessment confirmed that the ileus was not related to a mechanical obstruction. Management included intravenous fluids and conservative supportive care. Bowel sounds returned and the ileus resolved by day three of admission.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Ileus

Discharge Medications:
- Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea
- Liquid stool softener

Follow-up: Follow-up with primary care physician in 7 days for symptom monitoring.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, MD
05/15/2026

distractors.why: It is an ileus, not a mechanical obstruction.
